answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post titled 'NVIDIA Unlocks AI Compute at Scale, Inviting Partners to Power the AI Infrastructure Buildout', published and dated 2026-07-01. It is a party statement by the covered company, with a supporting quote from Sharon AI's CEO James Manning and a Firmus Technologies co-CEO quote, both relayed through NVIDIA's post.
answer.note: NVIDIA states it is introducing a new business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure and sell NVIDIA-powered cloud services to AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, supported by a revenue-sharing and credit-support model. Per NVIDIA, it would earn standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, giving it what it describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. This is a company description of its intended model and is not evidence of realized revenue, adoption levels, or contract terms. Conditionally, if the model is adopted at scale, it would shift part of NVIDIA's economics toward usage-linked cloud revenue and could increase its exposure to the financing and credit terms it extends to AI clouds. The Firmus Batam campus (expected up to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) is a developer's expected build-out, relevant as a supply and demand lead for NVIDIA accelerators, but it does not establish how many of those GPUs NVIDIA would sell directly or the timing of any purchases. Sharon AI and the other named AI natives (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) are named as participants or demand examples without disclosed purchase amounts, so they inform the model's reach rather than quantifying NVIDIA revenue.
limitations: The revenue-share percentage, its duration, and how cloud revenue on supported capacity is measured are not disclosed.
The size, form, and terms of the credit-support commitments NVIDIA would provide are not disclosed, so NVIDIA's contingent financial exposure cannot be sized from this source.
No signed agreements, purchase commitments, or launch dates are disclosed for the named AI clouds; the source describes the partnership as taking shape without giving a status for each participant.
The Firmus Batam 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are expectations from the developer's plan, with no disclosed timeline, financing status, or confirmed NVIDIA order volume.
The source is NVIDIA's own promotional post, so its characterization of demand and economics is not independently verified.
follow_up: Review NVIDIA's next periodic SEC filing for disclosure of the revenue-sharing and credit-support arrangements, including any guarantees, commitments, or contingent liabilities tied to AI cloud partners.
Check Firmus Technologies and Sharon AI public announcements for the Batam campus timeline, financing close, and any disclosed GPU purchase or deployment schedule.
Check whether named AI natives (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) or other AI clouds disclose agreements with NVIDIA under this model and whether any quantify revenue-share or credit terms.
